verdict_reasoning: No P0/P1. Two confirmed P2 actionable findings: #3 (a prevented input on a controlled Field.Control now clears Form server errors and runs validation, which breaks the react#9023 workaround contract) and #1 (the controlled clearErrors path the PR's headline fix depends on has no test). One P2 design decision for maintainers (#2): code-driven resets and async loads now raise new validation errors. Fix order: decide #2 first, then fix #3 and add #1's test so both pin the callback's final shape.
intent: Make Field.Control sync controlled value prop changes (including programmatic ones such as clear buttons or form resets) into field state (filled, dirty, validity, pending async validation) via useValueChanged, matching sibling controls; register the String()-serialized controlled value so dirty comparison works for non-string values; make onChange own only the uncontrolled path; honor details.cancel() from onValueChange. Must not regress uncontrolled behavior, Form integration, validation modes, or initial-value/dirty/filled semantics.

findings.title: Controlled-path Form error clearing has no test
findings.suggested_fix: Add a FieldControl.test.tsx case with a module-level `const errors = { message: 'Server error' }` and `<Form errors={errors}><Field.Root name="message"><Field.Control value={value} onValueChange={setValue} /><Field.Error /></Field.Root><button onClick={() => setValue('x')}>set</button></Form>`. Assert that 'Server error' is present, then that it is gone after (a) `fireEvent.change(textbox, { target: { value: 'a' } })` and (b) a fresh render where only the button is clicked. The errors object must stay referentially stable, because an inline literal re-applies the error on every controlled rerender.
findings.why_it_matters: The PR says it fixes a bug where a resolved server error stayed visible after a programmatic change. Now that `onChange` returns early when the field is controlled, the `clearErrors(name)` call inside `useValueChanged` is the only thing that clears a `<Form errors>` entry for a controlled Field.Control. That covers user typing as well as programmatic changes. No test in the suite renders a controlled Field.Control inside a Form with `errors`. The only prevented/clear-errors test uses an uncontrolled control, and Form.test.tsx has no controlled Field.Control at all. Deleting line 110 would leave every test passing, while server errors would stick on every controlled input, including the typical react-hook-form/Formik setup. I confirmed the current behavior works with a scratch test. The Form `errors` object has to be referentially stable across renders, because an inline literal re-applies the error on every controlled rerender and makes the test fail for the wrong reason.

findings.title: Reset after successful submit surfaces required error on cleared field
findings.suggested_fix: Track user-originated values in onChange (userValueRef.current = inputValue before the isControlled early return). In the useValueChanged callback, for code-driven changes (serializedValue !== userValueRef.current), still update dirty, filled and clearErrors, but call validation.change only when fieldState.valid === false. Resolved errors still clear, while resets and async loads no longer raise new errors. This assumes maintainers do not want code-driven changes to raise new errors. It conflicts with the new 'syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically' test, so it needs a maintainer decision.
findings.why_it_matters: The PR names 'a form library reset' as a case it fixes, but a reset now leaves the field showing an error. Take a common contact form: a controlled required `Field.Control` inside `<Form onFormSubmit={() => setValue('')}>`. The user types, submits successfully, and the code clears the input. The field immediately gets aria-invalid and shows 'Constraints not satisfied'. That happens because the new sync path treats a change made from code exactly like a keystroke: `submitAttemptedRef` stays true after the submit, and `markedDirtyRef` stays true even after `setDirty(false)`, so `validation.change('')` publishes valueMissing. The same path also affects forms that load data after mount. With `validationMode="onChange"`, a value loaded from the server marks the field dirty (against the '' baseline captured at mount) and shows validation errors before the user has touched it. On base neither case changed validity or dirty state. Sibling controls behave the same way, but text inputs are where clear-on-submit and load-after-mount are most common. A fix is to validate code-driven changes only when that clears an existing error.

findings.title: Prevented input on a controlled control now clears server errors and validates
findings.suggested_fix: Before the controlled early return in onChange, add `if (event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented || details.isCanceled) blockedValueRef.current = inputValue;`. At the top of the useValueChanged callback, when blockedValueRef.current === serializedValue, clear the ref and update only dirty and filled, skipping clearErrors and validation.change. This mirrors NumberFieldInput's blockRevalidationRef. Add a controlled variant of the prevented-change test.
findings.first_evidence: packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:144-146 -- if (isControlled) { return; }  (runs before the gate at :153 `if (!event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented && !details.isCanceled) {`)
findings.why_it_matters: On base, an input event whose default was prevented did not clear Form server errors or run validation, in both controlled and uncontrolled mode. This is the react#9023 workaround that the existing test 'does not clear errors or validate when change is prevented' covers. The new `if (isControlled) return;` skips that `defaultPrevented` / `isCanceled` gate for controlled inputs. When the consumer's onValueChange stores the value, useValueChanged calls `clearErrors(name)` and `validation.change` without the check. As a result, a controlled field in a Form with `errors` loses its server error and runs the validator on a prevented input. The existing test only covers uncontrolled mode, so CI stays green. Recording the prevented value, as NumberField does with its `blockRevalidationRef`, would restore the contract.

triage_groups.title: Controlled sync callback treats every controlled value change as a user edit
triage_groups.context: The new useValueChanged callback (FieldControl.tsx:105-115) runs clearErrors(name) and validation.change for every controlled value change, whether it came from a keystroke, a prevented input, or code (reset/async load); only the uncontrolled onChange path keeps the defaultPrevented/isCanceled gate.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Decide #2 first (should code-driven changes validate or only clear stale errors?). Then fix #3 by recording blocked/prevented values in onChange before the controlled early return and skipping clearErrors/validation.change for them in the callback. Add #1's controlled Form-errors test alongside, so neither change silently drops the clearErrors call the PR's headline fix depends on.
triage_groups.why: All three touch the same callback and the same clearErrors/validation.change pair; the #2 decision determines the callback's shape that #3's fix and #1's test must pin.

residual_risks: Remounted controlled Field.Control with an empty value keeps a stale data-filled (FieldControl.tsx:99-103). A controlled control that remounts inside a persistent Field.Root (key change, or unmount -> setValue('') -> remount) with value '' keeps data-filled (and data-dirty) from the previous control, because the new mount effect only ever sets filled to true and useValueChanged never fires on mount; base cleared it via `hasExternalValue && valueProp === '' -> setFilled(false)`. Reproduced by correctness and julik-frontend-races scratch jsdom tests; narrow path, P3 at anchor 50 (below the confidence threshold). Fix: in the mount effect set filled both ways, e.g. setFilled(Boolean(validation.inputRef.current?.value)).

Submit-time Field.Root `validate` (and Form.actionsRef.validate) now receives the String()-serialized controlled value instead of the raw value (e.g. "5" instead of 5) because the control registers serializedValue. Consistent with change/blur paths, which already passed DOM strings, but it is an observable argument-type change the PR body does not mention; validators checking typeof or comparing arrays structurally change behavior (adversarial scratch repro; correctness concurs).
testing_gaps: No test covers the PR's claim that a programmatic controlled change supersedes a pending async validator for the old value (relies on commit() bumping validationCommitIdRef). Add: async validate pending for 'a', setValue('') from code, late result must not show. (julik-frontend-races, correctness)

No test asserts that a controlled value the consumer rejects (onValueChange that ignores the value) leaves data-dirty/data-filled unset and does not validate; a partial regression that moves setDirty/setFilled ahead of the `if (isControlled) return` guard would pass the suite. (testing)
